items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: I was playing trumpet, Snub Mosley was playing trombone and Godley was playing drums.

ctx.x: Alphonso Trent, yeah. He had a good band. He had Snub Mosley, trombone player Snub Mosley. He had a trumpet player, fantastic trumpet player named Chester Clark. He had a good drummer called A. G. Godley. I think you've heard about him.
Yeah, I've heard of him. Peanuts Holland?

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] He used to mention a drummer named A. G. Godley. [INTERVIEWEE] That’s right, he played with Alphonso Trent.

ctx.x: When you met him he was crazy and when I first met him he was crazy. That was years ago. But, a wonderful guy. He knew what he wanted to hear and he knew what he wanted to play. You accept it if you want to. If you didn’t, you didn’t have to but he was going to play it anyway. He was a great drummer.
He used to mention a drummer named A. G. Godley.
That’s right, he played with Alphonso Trent.
